passages.original: ipse a milite nihil accepit, cum tribunatus ageret, nihil accipi passus est. nam et imperator iam tribunos duos, quos constitit stellaturas accepisse, lapidibus obrui ab auxiliaribus iussit. Exstat epistula Severi, qua scribit ad Ragonium Celsum Gallias regentem: Miserum est ut imitari eius disciplinam militarem non possimus quem per bellum vicimus, milites tui vagantur, tribuni medio die lavant, pro tricliniis popinas habent, pro cubiculis meritoria;
passages.english: He himself accepted nothing from a soldier when he held the tribunate, and he did not allow anything to be accepted. For when he was already emperor he ordered two tribunes, who were proved to have taken *stellaturae* [perquisites deducted from the soldiers' rations], to be stoned to death by the auxiliaries. There survives a letter of Severus, in which he writes to Ragonius Celsus, governor of the Gauls: "It is a wretched thing that we cannot imitate the military discipline of the man whom we defeated in war. Your soldiers wander about, the tribunes bathe at midday, they have cookshops instead of dining-rooms, brothels instead of bedrooms;
passages.notes: *Stellaturae* is a rare term, apparently for illicit gains taken by officers from soldiers' rations or pay; its exact sense is uncertain. *Meritoria* may mean hired lodgings or brothels; "brothels" is chosen here from the context of dissipation.
